header: This is the SPELLING SAFETY NET for name searches (step 55b). WHY: the name search compares a typed word with a name word through a phonetic CODE (indic_fold): two spellings match only when their codes are EQUAL. That cannot reach 100%: the code can be taught Roy = Ray and Majumdar = Mazumder, but every new way to write a Bengali name ("Gosyami", "Gosami", "Goshami" for Goswami) is a new rule, and one word off in one name word dropped the person ("rupak gosyami" found nobody although "Rupak" was perfect). Rules alone will never close it. WHAT: when a name search finds NOBODY, I look at each name word of the SQL. A word that no real name is spelled (or coded) like is replaced by the NEAREST real name word of the directory, and the same SQL is run again, so every other condition of the question stays. The answer says so ("No name is spelled “Gosyami”: showing the nearest spelling, Goswami."). HOW NEAR: I compare the words by a key that treats W and Y after a consonant and before a vowel as silent (Goswami = Goshami = Gosyami = Gosami, Swapan, Biswas, Dwijen, Sandhya: the Bengali ব-ফলা and য-ফলা), then folded like the database does. Words that SOUND the same under that key are accepted; a weaker match must be one slip in the letters (two in a long word; a swapped pair of letters counts as one) AND keep the first sound. A word of fewer than 4 letters is never corrected. Only a word that is not already known (the same word, or the same code, as a real name) is touched, so a correct word is never "improved", and a question whose people simply do not exist stays empty (nothing is invented). No database change: the vocabulary is read from nlq.employees.name_words and kept for ten minutes.

symbols.name: withoutGlides
doc: W or Y after a consonant and before a vowel is silent in a Bengali name (Goswami = Goshami = Gosyami), so I drop it.

symbols.name: spellingKey
doc: This is the key that two spellings of one name share.

symbols.name: databaseCodes
doc: The code the database itself gives a word (what nlq.word_like compares), for either position; I need the same codes here.

symbols.name: editDistance
symbols.sig: export function editDistance(a: string, b: string): number
doc: Edit distance in which a swap of two neighbouring letters counts as ONE slip (rupak / rupka).

members.name: words
doc: every distinct name word (letters only, upper case, at least 3 letters)

members.name: codes
doc: the database codes of the words: a typed word with one of these codes is already found by the phonetic match

symbols.name: buildVocabulary
symbols.sig: export function buildVocabulary(rows: { w: string; n: number }[]): NameVocabulary

symbols.name: isKnownWord
symbols.sig: export function isKnownWord(token: string, vocab: NameVocabulary): boolean
doc: A word the name search already finds: the same word as a real name, or one with the same code.

symbols.name: candidateWords
symbols.sig: export function candidateWords(token: string, vocab: NameVocabulary): Nearest[]
doc: Every real name word that a typed word could mean, the best first. I accept a candidate when it SOUNDS the same under the key (distance 0: strong evidence), or when the key is near AND the letters are one slip away, or when the letters alone are one slip away (two in a word of 9+ letters) and the first sound is the same: the key collapses vowels, so one missing letter can look like a distance of 2 or 3 there (KUMA / KUMAR). A different first sound is a different name ("swapan" is not "tapan"); the first two letters swapped ("raup" / "arup") is one slip. I return nothing for a known word (the phonetic search already finds it) or a word of fewer than 4 letters.

symbols.name: nearestWords
symbols.sig: export function nearestWords(token: string, vocab: NameVocabulary, max = 3): Nearest[]
doc: The real name words NEAREST to a typed word: the best tier only, at most `max`; I return nothing when the word is equally near to MORE than `max` names (then any choice would be a guess). A name that is simply not in the directory must stay "not found" and never become somebody else.

symbols.name: nameLiteralsIn
doc: Finds nlq.word_like(name_words, name_codes, 'x') and its first_/last_ forms, and the exact form 'X' = ANY(name_words).

symbols.name: correctSql
symbols.sig: export function correctSql(sql: string, vocab: NameVocabulary): { sql: string; changes: SpellingChange[] } | null
doc: Returns the SQL with every unknown name word replaced by its nearest real spelling(s); null when nothing was changed.

symbols.name: spellingNote
doc: Builds the sentence under the answer.

symbols.name: WithClient
doc: ---- the vocabulary of the directory and the second search ---------------------------------------

symbols.name: cache
symbols.sig: let cache: { at: number; vocab: NameVocabulary } | null = null

symbols.name: directoryNameWords
symbols.sig: export async function directoryNameWords(withClient: WithClient): Promise<string[]>
doc: The name words of the directory (letters only, upper case, at least 3 letters), for the search bar's "looks like a name" hint: I give the words only, with nobody attached. Kept for ten minutes, like the rest.

symbols.name: spellingRetry
symbols.sig: export async function spellingRetry(sql: string, deps: { withClient: WithClient; exec?: ExecOptions }): Promise<{ sql: string; data: QueryResultData; note: string } | null>
symbols.returns: Promise<{ sql: string; data: QueryResultData; note: string } | null>
doc: The second search: the same SQL with the nearest real spellings. It gives null when nothing could be corrected or when the corrected SQL finds nobody either.

behaviours: Goswami, Goshami, Gosyami, Gosami share one key
Swapan = Sapan, Biswas = Bishwas = Bisas, Dwijen = Dijen, Sandhya = Sandha
a w or y at the start of a word, or before a consonant, is kept: Wasim, Yash, Kumari
different names do not share a key: Goswami / Banerjee, Tapan / Saran
edit distance: equal, one slip, a swap, an insertion
"${t}" is Goswami
'gosamy' (the vowel and the glide both off) is Goswami too
one slip: 'goswmi' (a letter missing) is Goswami
'rupk' and 'rupka' are Rupak
'goswamy', 'gosvami', 'goswamee' are KNOWN: the phonetic search already finds them, nothing is changed
a real word is never 'improved': every word of the directory is known and has no correction
a short word is never corrected (fewer than 4 letters)
a different first sound is a different name: 'swapan' is not 'tapan' or 'saran'
a word far from every name stays as it is: 'abcdefgh', 'zzzzzz', 'quentin'
names that are different families are not merged: 'singh' stays known, 'sinha' stays known, 'banerji' goes to Banerjee only
a tie keeps both candidates (at most three): 'karmakr' is Karmakar or Karmaker
a missing letter: 'kuma' is Kumar, 'snjay' is Sanjay, 'majumdr' is Majumdar or Majumder (a tie: both kept)
'sanjy' sounds like Sanjay AND Sanjoy: it is KNOWN (the phonetic search finds both), so the net leaves it alone
two letters swapped: 'rupka' is Rupak, 'sakrar' is Sarkar, 'goswmai' is Goswami
the first two letters swapped is one slip too: 'raup' is Arup
but any other change of the first letter is a different name: 'sarup' is not 'arup'
equally near to MORE than three names: nothing is guessed
candidateWords lists everything that could be meant, the best first: 'soen' is SEN, then SOMEN and SOREN
...but only the best is searched: nearestWords('soen') is SEN
the corrected SQL searches SEN only; SOMEN and SOREN are only named in the note
the note says so: 'also close: Somen or Soren'
a tie is searched in full and has nothing 'also close' to add: 'somn' is Somen or Soman
an unknown word with only one candidate has nothing 'also close': 'gosyami'
the two helper calls are found, with their words
all three helpers and the exact form are found
SQL with no name word has nothing to correct
'Gosyami' becomes GOSWAMI; 'Rupak' (known) is untouched; the rest of the SQL is the same
two unknown words are both corrected: 'Rupk' -> RUPAK, 'Gosami' -> GOSWAMI
a tie becomes an OR of the candidates, each in its own call
the exact form 'X' = ANY(name_words) is corrected too
a known word, a short word and a word with a space are left alone (nothing to correct: null)
the corrected SQL still has exactly the shape the guard expects (one SELECT, no semicolon or comment)
the note names the typed word and the nearest spelling
two words, and a tie
Datta, Datt, Dutt and Dutta share one code
...and stay different from Dey, Dhar, Datar and Dattatreya
a typed Dutta is a known word when the directory has only Datta
the pattern of the rule touches Datta and Datt as whole words only
no name word in the SQL: no search, no database
a name word in the SQL needs the directory's names: a database failure surfaces (the pipeline then keeps the first answer)
